title: Majority Element II
spaceBreakdown:
- cand1, cand2, cnt1, cnt2, v1, v2, n: scalars → O(1)
- res: returned output (not counted)
- no recursion, no containers
approach: At most two elements can appear more than ⌊n/3⌋ times, so we track two candidate/count pairs. In one pass, each element either boosts a matching candidate, claims an empty slot, or decrements both counts (pairing it against two "enemies"). Any true majority survives because it has too many copies to be fully cancelled. A second pass verifies actual frequencies, since candidates may be stale.
hints: At most how many distinct values can each occupy more than ⌊n/3⌋ of the n positions? The array can be up to 5·10⁴ long.
Boyer-Moore Majority Vote with two candidate slots. On [3,2,3]: 3 fills slot1 (count 1), 2 fills slot2 (count 1), final 3 bumps slot1 to count 2; then verify each candidate's real frequency.

```
cand1 = None, cand2 = None, cnt1 = 0, cnt2 = 0
for x in nums:
    if x == cand1:  cnt1 += 1
    elif x == cand2: cnt2 += 1
    elif cnt1 == 0: cand1, cnt1 = x, 1
    elif cnt2 == 0: cand2, cnt2 = x, 1
    else: cnt1 -= 1; cnt2 -= 1
count actual occurrences of cand1, cand2
return those with count > n/3
```

**No majority** - three distinct values each appear once.
`Input: nums = [1,2,3]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: returning candidates without a verification pass → returns [1,2]

**Threshold boundary** - one value appears exactly twice in four elements.
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,3]` → `Expected: [3]`
⚠️ Bug: using `count >= n/3` instead of `count > n/3` → returns [3,2]

**Two qualifying elements** - both values appear once in a length-2 array.
`Input: nums = [1,2]` → `Expected: [1,2]`
⚠️ Bug: using single-candidate majority vote (the n/2 version) → returns [1]

**Value equals initial candidate** - the sole element is 0, same as the default candidate.
`Input: nums = [0]` → `Expected: [0]`
⚠️ Bug: using two separate `if` statements (not `else if`) in verification when both candidates start at 0 → returns [0,0]

followUps.q: Generalize to finding all elements appearing more than ⌊n/k⌋ times.
followUps.a: Maintain k−1 candidate/count pairs with the same pairing-down logic: match, claim empty slot, or decrement all. Verify in a second pass. TC: O(n·k), SC: O(k).

followUps.q: The input is a stream you can read only once - no second pass for verification.
followUps.a: Keep a hash map of counts capped at k−1 entries: increment on match, add on new key, and when size exceeds k−1 decrement all and drop zeros. TC: O(n), SC: O(k).

followUps.q: Find elements appearing more than (n/3 ± ε) times in a stream too large to store.
followUps.a: Replace exact counts with a Count-Min Sketch; query each candidate's estimated frequency and compare to the relaxed threshold. TC: O(n), SC: O(1/ε · log(1/δ)).
